frameworks.name: Free Trial Conversion Architecture
frameworks.definition: A multi-stage analysis comparing free trial vs paid-first models across three vectors: landing page conversion, paid conversion rate, and post-trial churn.

frameworks.name: Earnings-Per-Click Model
frameworks.definition: A decision framework that factors clicks, conversion rate, customer LTV, and churn into a single unit-economics calculation to compare acquisition models.

claims.text: Free trials increase initial landing-page conversion while decreasing subsequent paid conversion, creating two conversion points instead of one (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: where free access can be granted upfront
claims.mechanism: Offering free access removes friction on the initial decision but creates a second friction point where a customer must commit payment after experiencing the product.

claims.text: Post-trial churn is lower than month-one churn from paid-first acquisition because customers have already experienced the product before committing (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Trial experience reduces perceived risk and commitment hesitation, anchoring customers before the first renewal decision.

claims.text: To decide between free-trial and paid-first models, build a spreadsheet comparing: clicks to page, trial-conversion rate, paid-conversion rate, LTV by model, and churn by model; the model with higher total revenue is the winner (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when choosing between two acquisition models
when sufficient data exists for both paths
claims.mechanism: Quantifying all three vectors (landing-page conversion, paid conversion, churn-driven LTV) makes the comparison falsifiable and removes emotion from the decision.

anchors.region: 4x click conversion increase with 50% paid conversion
4x click conversion increase with 66% paid conversion
4x click conversion increase with 75% paid conversion

bounded_by: Does not apply when insufficient data or runway exists to measure both full cycles

claims.text: Free trials succeed or fail based on earnings-per-click: the cost to generate a click must account for both the increased landing-page conversion (free CTA) and the downstream paid conversion and LTV (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when comparing paid-first and free-trial acquisition
when click source cost is measurable (organic or paid)
claims.mechanism: A free CTA generates more clicks than a paid CTA because the initial ask is lower; this increases cost-per-sale unless the higher volume compounds downstream revenue.

claims.text: When 4x more customers convert to a free trial than to a paid offer, the business doubles sales even if two-thirds of trial users cancel before paying, because the cost of acquisition is distributed across remaining customers (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: free-trial model with measurable conversion lift
when cancel rate on free trial is pre-measured

numbers.axis: trial-to-paying conversion outcome by cancel rate

claims.text: Do not back out of a free-trial test before collecting at least one full billing cycle of data, because early exit prevents discovering whether the economics work or not (Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when churn data is needed to finalize the decision
claims.mechanism: One month is the minimum window to capture trial-to-paid conversion and initial churn; exiting early leaves the experiment inconclusive.
bounded_by: Does not apply if the business cannot sustain the experiment cost for one full cycle

examples.text: Alex Hormozi's portfolio company (School HQ) experienced 4x conversion increase when offering a free trial compared to paid-first model, generating 40 customers per day in the first week. The speaker generated 100k followers across YouTube and Instagram in four months with a free community product, then offered paid continuity upsells.

A speaker's experiment with free trials on a group offer showed high initial conversion but some immediate cancellation post-trial. When modeled: at 4x landing conversion and 50% paid-trial conversion, the business still doubled sales despite trial cancellation.

practices.text: Use earnings-per-click as the decision unit: track clicks to landing page, trial-conversion percentage, paid-conversion percentage, and LTV by model.
Run the free-trial experiment for at least one full month before making a go/no-go decision on churn and economics.
Build a spreadsheet comparing free-trial and paid-first models with all three vectors (landing conversion, paid conversion, churn-driven LTV) to remove emotion from the decision.
